title: Real filings: no invented figures, and 'not filed' is not zero
summary: When an LLM summarises or import a real accounting filing it must record exactly what the filing states. An intentionally omitted statement is evidence of omission, not of a zero; and a filed-accounts import never posts to the native going-concern ledger. Missing assurance on an arithmetic computation is not treated as a confidence in invented detail.
evidence_note: v0.2 locked 'a filed-accounts import never posts to the native GL' and locked the rule that 'not filed != zero' semantics for intentionally omitted Income Statements. REAL_FILING_16024067_QUALIFICATION records that a filing states the Income Statement was not delivered; the assessment retains the profit fact found elsewhere without pretending the absent detail exists.
invariants: Do not invent a figure the filing did not deliver, even to make a review read cleanly.
'Not presented in the filing' is recorded as an omission fact, never coerced to zero.
An external financial-statement assessment keeps its own book separate from the native ledger.
When a figure is asserted from a derived computation, bind it to the source figures and arithmetic profile instead of asserting authority you do not hold.
